text:
tasha: Heads-up — NimbleCart on dedicated-eu-west-2 reports lots of 429s and intermittent latency spikes since 09:14 UTC. Customer says traffic spikes then things autoscale but requests still get throttled. Can SRE look?

sre-bot: [ALERT] 09:16 UTC autoscaler: oscillation detected for pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-queue1 (scale_count=6 in 18m). Related incidents: none.

jonathan: I'll grab logs. @maria can you pull the autoscaler events and recent pool metrics?

maria: grabbing now. quick summary: scale up/down churn ~ every 2-4 minutes for that pool. queue_depth spikes to ~120 then drains quickly, but our scale-down cooldown is 90s and scale-up reacts at 60s — looks like thresholds and cooldowns are too tight for bursty queue pattern. CPU/GPU usage flat ~40% most of the time.

vikram: i suspect a short-lived burst pattern + aggressive downscale. when queue spikes we scale up, then queue drains, then quickly scale down -> next burst sees no warm capacity so latency/429s during spin-up.

maria: exact autoscaler events (excerpt):
```
[09:12:04] scale_up initiated pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-queue1 reason="queue_depth>100" -> target=6
[09:14:10] scale_down initiated pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-queue1 reason="util<0.5" -> target=3
[09:16:20] scale_up initiated pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-queue1 reason="queue_depth>90" -> target=6
[09:18:35] scale_down initiated pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-queue1 reason="util<0.5" -> target=2
```

jonathan: that pattern fits noisy-burst-induced flap. any signs of a single tenant hammering?

maria: Tenant-level metrics show multiple tenants contributing; no single noisy neighbor. request rate shape is many short bursts from the same customer segment (cart totalization jobs) — probably client retry pattern.

tasha: NimbleCart says they do short heavy bursts at checkout times, and they triggered client retry logic when they saw 429s which amplified the bursts. They want a quick mitigation.

vikram: mitigation options: 1) increase scale-down cooldown to 300s (5m) so we don't drop capacity between bursts; 2) introduce a short warm standby (min_replicas=3 -> 4) for that pool; 3) add prefix/KV cache or local queue smoothing; 4) bump scale-up to pre-warm an extra instance earlier.

maria: I'd prefer non-invasive: bump scale-down cooldown to 300s + add conservative min_replicas for this tenant's pool. should reduce 429s quickly. Also add a rate-limit bucket for the customer to flatten retries.

jonathan: agree. config diff to test:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  pool: dedicated-eu-west-2-queue1
  scale_up_threshold: 80  # keep
  scale_down_cooldown_secs: 300
  min_replicas: 3  # was 2
  fast_scale_up_enabled: true
```

maria: i'll apply to canary region and monitor. what about billing/commit impact? tasha, pls confirm with customer that this will keep extra warm capacity and could increase billed reserved usage a bit while we stabilize.

tasha: will ping NimbleCart and ask permission for temporary warmening. also opening support ticket SR-18421 and noting potential cost impact.

sre-bot: [CHANGE] 09:28 UTC autoscaler config updated in staging (scale_down_cooldown_secs=300, min_replicas=3) by maria.

maria: deployed to canary pool. watching telemetry. initial 10m shows queue spikes handled w/o 429s, scale events reduced from 6->2 in window.

nicole: thanks all — i'll coordinate CS note to NimbleCart: explain warm capacity and suggest client retry backoff + jitter as long term fix.

maria: next steps: 1) keep cooldown=300s for 24h and monitor error budget; 2) if stable, roll to prod pools; 3) add an autoscale policy that uses queue_derivative (ramp rate) rather than raw depth to avoid reacting to very short spikes; 4) follow-up postmortem with recommended tenant-side retry guidance.

jonathan: will add a short repro script to run against canary so CS can validate:
```bash
# slam the pool with short bursts to reproduce
for i in {1..6}; do
  seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P50 curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  sleep 20
done
```

maria: nice — that'll validate. leaving this on my plate. ping here if you see fresh 429s.

tasha: customer informed, they approved temporary warm capacity. marking SR-18421 as in-progress. :thumbsup:

vikram: once stable we'll consider a more sophisticated controller: hysteresis + prediction model for bursty tenants. for now cooldown tweak + min_replicas is lowest-risk.

maria: closing loop in 24h with metrics snapshot and recommended config. thanks team.
